items.name: Eran Guy
items.title: Principal Asic Engineer, Hardware Engineering.
items.testimonial:
Rules make sense most of the time. Until they don't.

When we weigh Jensen's extraordinary contributions, the allegations against him, and the punishment imposed, we are left with a disturbing picture of injustice and a profound failure of moral judgment.

I ask every board member: Do you truly believe, in your heart, that Jensen deserves to be pushed out of the company he built from the ground up with his own bare hands, a company to which he devoted his life and through which he has touched so many of ours?

Is this truly what justice looks like?

Or will you silence your conscience with the convenient, inexcusable justification that "these are the rules of the game"?

Rules are meant to serve justice, not replace our moral judgment.

And morality demands more than blindly following rules. It demands the courage to question them when they lead us to injustice.

items.testimonial:
I want Jensen back as NVIDIA’s CEO for the following reasons:
* Whatever mistakes he may have made in his personal life are between him, his family, and the other people involved. It is not our place to pass moral judgment. Let those affected resolve their private matters among themselves.
* NVIDIA would not have become the world’s most valuable company without Jensen pouring his blood, sweat, and countless sleepless nights into building it over 33 years.
* With all due respect to potential successors, I am convinced that no one else could lead NVIDIA as effectively in its current form - running the business, nurturing its ecosystem, and inventing the future.
* Provided Jensen is cleared of any allegations of knowingly sharing national security secrets or facilitating violations of export controls, I see no reason not to reinstate him as CEO.

My position is simple: judge his leadership on its merits, let the people involved handle their private affairs, and base any decision about his return on established facts rather than speculation.

I’m adding my name to this letter in support of bringing Jensen back.

Jensen is a visionary leader. He saw possibilities long before the rest of us did, and he had the conviction to pursue them when it wasn’t easy or popular. Much of what we’ve built and become carries his fingerprints. His contributions to this team, to the work, and to the people around him can’t be overstated, and they won’t be forgotten.

He also deserved a better goodbye. After everything he gave, he should have been thanked and honored properly, and his departure should have reflected the respect he earned. That didn’t happen, and it still weighs on those of us who worked alongside him.

Bringing Jensen back would do right by someone who gave so much. It would also bring back the vision, the leadership, and the spirit that made this a place worth being part of.

I sincerely request the NVIDIA board and leadership to reconsider bringing back Jensen and giving him another opportunity to contribute to the company's future.

We are all human, and everyone makes mistakes. Nobody is perfect. Forgiveness, understanding, and second chances are important values. Difficult situations should be handled fairly, and personal circumstances should be considered separately from the company's business interests and growth.

Jensen is more than just a leader; he is a pillar and backbone of NVIDIA's remarkable journey. He helped build NVIDIA from the ground up and played a historic role in transforming it into one of the world's leading technology companies. His vision, dedication, and contribution are deeply connected to NVIDIA's identity and success.

A true visionary remains a visionary despite challenges and setbacks. Years of dedication should never be overshadowed by difficult circumstances. His experience, vision, and leadership deserve recognition and consideration.

I understand the board has responsibilities and must make difficult decisions. However, I hope it will also reflect on his immense contribution to building NVIDIA. It is genuinely sad to see someone who played such a significant role become separated from the company's leadership and board.

Can we reconsider, forgive, rebuild, and create a new chapter together? I request the board to stand by him and explore the possibility of bringing him back.

We want NVIDIA to continue innovating, growing, and leading the world. We miss Jensen's leadership and vision and hope to see him contribute to NVIDIA's next chapter.

Our mission should always come first, but let us not forget the visionary who helped build its foundation.

We believe in NVIDIA, its future, and Jensen. Let's rebuild together!

Even if aspects of Jensen’s private life are morally questionable, his professional leadership and business achievements should be evaluated on their own merits. Under his leadership, the company has grown tremendously, and its success speaks for itself. Personal matters should not automatically dictate professional decisions unless they directly affect the company’s integrity, governance, or performance.

Forcing him to resign based on suspicion or unsubstantiated allegations involving a woman is neither fair nor a sound basis for judgment. Suspicion is not proof, and personal controversy should not overshadow years of demonstrated leadership and achievement.

If his leadership remains effective and there is no substantiated evidence of professional misconduct, he deserves a fair and objective assessment—not a premature condemnation.

Let business performance be judged by business standards, personal conduct by ethical standards, and allegations by evidence. He deserves the opportunity to return.

NVDA Shareholder Coalition — Statement of Purpose

We are exploring the formation of an independent coalition of NVIDIA shareholders focused on long-term shareholder value, leadership continuity, and accountable corporate governance.

We believe Jensen Huang’s extraordinary contributions to NVIDIA warrant a thorough, fair, and independent assessment of whether he could be considered for a future leadership role, subject to the findings of ongoing investigations and all applicable legal and compliance requirements.

We call on NVIDIA’s Board of Directors to:

1. Conduct a thorough and independent review of the relevant facts.
2. Evaluate all qualified CEO candidates using transparent, shareholder-focused criteria, including Jensen Huang if legally and ethically appropriate.
3. Protect NVIDIA’s long-term technological leadership, customer trust, and shareholder interests.
4. Provide shareholders with appropriate information about the CEO succession process.

Our initiative is independent of NVIDIA and does not represent the company or its employees.

This statement is not a solicitation of proxies or a request for voting authority. Any future shareholder action will be subject to applicable securities laws and legal review.

items.name: Le Lu
items.testimonial:
Dear Jensen and the NVIDIA Board,

My journey with NVIDIA began during my university years, when I first studied molecular dynamics and discovered how GPGPU computing could accelerate simulations of large molecular systems. That realization was a turning point in my scientific life - a personal singularity that fundamentally changed how I imagined the possibilities of computational science.

Since then, I have grown alongside NVIDIA's remarkable technological evolution. Each new generation of computing technology has empowered me to explore problems that once seemed beyond reach, pushing the boundaries of what I could learn, simulate, and create.

Today, I am fortunate to work at the heart of advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Looking back, I realize how profoundly NVIDIA's innovations - and Jensen Huang's vision and leadership - have indirectly shaped my journey as a scientist and engineer.

Jensen, you may never know how many researchers like me have been inspired and empowered by what you have built. Your impact extends far beyond products, companies, or financial results. You have helped expand the horizons of scientific possibility for an entire generation.

I sincerely hope the Board will approach this matter with fairness, transparency, and evidence-based judgment, while recognizing the extraordinary legacy of innovation and inspiration that Jensen represents.

Thank you, Jensen, for helping make the seemingly impossible possible.

These views are expressed solely in my personal capacity and do not represent my employer.

items.name: Andy Huang
items.testimonial:
I stand with Jensen Huang.

Serious allegations deserve serious investigation, not trial by media. Before any conclusions are drawn or actions taken, there must be a thorough, independent, and transparent examination of the facts, with due process and a fair opportunity for all parties to respond.

The New York Times has a responsibility to report facts, not construct narratives that encourage the public to reach a verdict before the evidence has been fully examined. Journalism should hold power accountable, but it should never appoint itself judge and jury.

Accountability matters. So do fairness, evidence, and the presumption of innocence. These principles must apply to everyone, regardless of their position or public profile.

I support Jensen Huang’s right to a fair and impartial process. Let the facts determine the outcome, not headlines or public pressure.

items.testimonial:
I've been with NVIDIA for 21 years. I still remember the first time I met Jensen, many years ago, when he visited our Moscow office.

What surprised me most was how remarkably down-to-earth he was. Here was the CEO of a company already changing the technology industry, yet he came across as a regular, approachable person. That impression stayed with me.

Over the years, I've witnessed NVIDIA navigate some incredibly difficult situations. What consistently stood out to me was the effort to do right by employees, even when the circumstances were beyond the company's control.

One example I'll never forget is the closure of our Moscow office in 2022.

While many companies had already left Russia, NVIDIA continued supporting its employees for as long as it could. When the office finally had to close, employees were offered the opportunity to relocate to another country where NVIDIA had an office, or receive a generous severance package.

A person's legacy is bigger than any single headline.

items.testimonial:
AN OPEN LETTER TO THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF NVIDIA
We stand at a defining moment in technological history, and at its center is NVIDIA—a company whose name is synonymous with the future. At the heart of NVIDIA is Jensen Huang.
Today, external noise surrounding private matters threatens to overshadow decades of historic achievement. As shareholders, employees, and global supporters, we issue this urgent appeal to the Board of Directors: Do not allow private affairs to interfere with corporate governance. Stand firmly behind Jensen Huang, for NVIDIA is great because of him.
From a rational standpoint, separating a leader's personal life from their professional stewardship is the foundation of sound governance. A CEO's private affairs, entirely unrelated to fiduciary duty or operational execution, must never become grounds for destabilizing a multi-trillion-dollar enterprise. NVIDIA’s dominance is no accident; it is the result of Jensen’s unmatched vision in CUDA and accelerated computing. Jeopardizing his leadership over non-business matters is economically irrational and strategically catastrophic.
Yet beyond logic lies the undeniable humanity of the man behind the leather jacket. Those who know Jensen see a deeply warm, compassionate leader who remembers the names of frontline engineers and uplifts young researchers. Forged in a Denny’s in 1993, NVIDIA survived decades of near-collapse only because Jensen stood shoulder-to-shoulder with his team, sharing every burden with unwavering care and resilience.
History reminds us that George Washington was indispensable to the survival and unity of the early United States. Just as Washington is to America, Jensen Huang is to NVIDIA—the living architect who built an empire from a dream.
If this Board is truly wise and reasonable, there is only one path forward: Protect our company’s stability, honor its legacy, and stand unequivocally behind the legendary CEO who made NVIDIA great.
Respectfully submitted,
Hao Ting Li

items.name: Huaichen Yang
items.testimonial:
The allegations are serious, and they should be examined carefully. But so far they are only allegations. No charges have been filed, and no findings have been made public. Due process and the presumption of innocence should apply to Mr. Huang just as they apply to every American. Neither the media nor political pressure should deliver the verdict before the facts are in.

What is at stake goes far beyond one company. Over three decades, Mr. Huang built the computing platform that powers nearly every major AI breakthrough. His vision and his technical judgment are a strategic asset to the United States at a moment when our global AI leadership is being fiercely contested. Losing that leadership on the basis of unproven claims would be a self-inflicted wound to American competitiveness.

If any regulatory or security gaps are found, they should be fixed through clear rules and stronger oversight. Making an example of an individual does not fix them. If the investigation clears Mr. Huang, the Board should give serious consideration to restoring his leadership role.

America should hold its leaders accountable. It should also protect the people who have helped make this country the world leader in technology. Please let the facts, not politics, decide this outcome.

items.testimonial:
You Cannot Simply Replace Jensen Huang

I have watched NVIDIA’s extraordinary rise with genuine admiration. Every breakthrough, every new achievement, every seemingly impossible milestone was a reason to celebrate. Not just because of the company’s success, but because of the remarkable man behind it.

Jensen Huang is not simply a CEO. He is a founder, a visionary, and one of the most brilliant minds of our time.

He believed in a future that others could not yet imagine. He took risks when others doubted him. He spent 33 years building a company that would eventually transform the world.

And now, we are expected to accept that a man who created something so extraordinary can simply be removed from the company he devoted his life to?

I find that deeply troubling.

Of course, no one should be above the law or beyond accountability. But fairness matters. Evidence matters. And a lifetime of extraordinary achievement deserves more than a hasty judgment.

I am not an NVIDIA employee. I am simply someone who has admired Jensen Huang, celebrated NVIDIA’s achievements, and believed in the future he was building.

I hope the Board of Directors understands that this is about more than a corporate position. It is about leadership, loyalty, vision, and the human being behind one of the greatest technological achievements of our generation.

Please reconsider this decision. Let the facts be established fairly, and give Jensen Huang the opportunity to continue what he started.

You can replace a title. You can replace a position. But you cannot replace the mind that imagined the future before the rest of the world could see it.

Stand with Jensen.

Dear Members of the NVIDIA Board of Directors,

I am a NVIDIA shareholder writing to express my full support for Jensen Huang.

items.name: John L
items.testimonial:
To the Board:
I write as an NVDA shareholder. What concerns me is not sentiment about a founder. It is the growth trajectory of the company I own.
Jensen Huang is not interchangeable with any successor. The AI era was not handed to NVIDIA. It was built by a CEO who made early, unpopular, capital-intensive bets on accelerated computing years before the market agreed, and who then held the company to that direction through multiple cycles where the bet looked wrong. That kind of conviction is not a skillset you recruit. It is thirty years of accumulated judgment about which technical directions are dead ends and which are the future.
Removing him mid-cycle has a concrete cost. Strategy at this company is inseparable from the person who has been making the calls, and any successor takes time to earn the confidence of partners, customers and the internal teams who execute on those bets. In a market moving as fast as AI, that transition period is not neutral. It is measured in lost design wins, delayed roadmaps, and competitors closing gaps that were not close a year ago.
I am not asking the Board to ignore an investigation. I am asking it to explain why removal before that investigation reports serves the company's growth, and to answer publicly what was established and when.
Shareholders are not asking for reassurance. We are asking for the record.
Thank you.

items.testimonial:
I'm a shareholder of NVIDIA, and I support bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO.
Jensen built this company over 33 years — from a graphics chip startup into the engine of the AI era. That record is not erased by a personal failing. What he has admitted is infidelity, not any transfer of information; the espionage allegation remains unproven, and no one has been charged. A personal matter should not be the reason to remove a founder-CEO, especially while the board's own independent investigation is still unfinished.
If the investigation finds real wrongdoing that harms the company, that is a different conversation — with evidence, a fair hearing, and a reasoned decision. Until then, removing him without due process hurts employees, shareholders, and the company he built. Bring Jensen back.

items.name: Wenjun Shi

items.testimonial: Jensen Huang built the compute foundation of American AI supremacy: he made the 2007 bet on CUDA that turned the GPU into the engine of AI, and virtually every U.S. frontier model,  from OpenAI to Anthropic to Meta  was trained on NVIDIA chips under his leadership. When Washington imposed export controls in 2022 to blunt Beijing's AI ambitions, that policy worked only because America held an unmatchable lead in cutting-edge silicon — a lead that exists because of his three-decade architecture of NVIDIA's technology. His chips are now core U.S. defense assets, running in the Air Force's DGX supercomputers and the platforms of defense leaders like Anduril. From the $500 billion Stargate data centers to "Sovereign AI" infrastructure he has exported to allied nations across the Gulf, Europe, and Asia, Huang's company is the keystone of the allied AI coalition the United States is assembling against China. Lose him, and America risks losing not just a CEO, but the strategic advantage in AI, silicon, and deterrence on which its position against China rests.

We, the undersigned, respectfully urge Nvidia's Board of Directors to invite Jensen Huang back as President and CEO.

In 1993, Jensen co-founded Nvidia at a Denny's table with a small team and a big idea. Over more than three decades, he turned it into one of the most transformative companies in the world. He led the invention of the GPU, bet on CUDA when few others saw its potential, and positioned Nvidia at the heart of the AI revolution.

He has been recognized as one of the world's best CEOs, but what sets him apart is the culture he built: relentless curiosity, a willingness to take on hard problems, and deep loyalty to the engineers, partners, and customers who made Nvidia great. He has inspired a generation of innovators and set a standard for visionary leadership.

Nvidia's mission is far from finished. We believe Jensen's vision, experience, and passion are irreplaceable, and that his return would restore confidence and momentum for employees, shareholders, and the industry.

We ask the Board to bring Jensen Huang home.

You have accepted the resignation of the mind that built your company and called it governance. I call it what it is: caretakers voting out the man whose judgment created everything you now guard. For thirty-three years Jensen Huang bet his own reasoning against the industry’s consensus and was proven right, and no committee, interim title, or search firm can produce the vision you just showed the door. Investigate whatever you must and require whatever safeguards the facts call for, but judge the man by what he built, not by what his enemies hope to make of him. — John Galt

items.testimonial:
Jensen’s value to NVIDIA goes far beyond that of a conventional CEO—he is the irreplaceable linchpin of the entire global AI and semiconductor ecosystem.   First, NVIDIA’s supply chain resilience is built on Jensen’s personal trust and leadership. Across Taiwan, mainland China, South Korea, and Southeast Asia, he personally bridged decades-old rivalries among hardware titans—bringing fierce competitors to the same table, sharing margins generously, and backing emerging cloud partners. That level of loyalty and coordination cannot be inherited by a successor.   Second, NVIDIA’s technological moat exists because Jensen defied short-term Wall Street pressure. Back in 2009, when GPU computing was dismissed and shareholders questioned CUDA, Jensen stood firm and personally traveled to university labs around the world—donating hardware, courses, and training with no strings attached to inspire a generation of researchers.   

To the Board: you CANNOT simply drop in a new executive and expect them to replicate decades of cross-cultural trust, supply-chain orchestration, developer evangelism, and long-term technical conviction. Removing Jensen without due process threatens the very foundation of what makes NVIDIA extraordinary. Thank you, Jensen—we stand with you.

items.testimonial:
Jensen and members of the board,

I’m Henry Herrera, founder of GridFleet LLC, recently accepted into NVIDIA Inception. I’m building The Grid, an agentic AI platform that brings together specialized agents, persistent memory, and tools to help people and businesses get real work done, with human oversight built in.

After more than 16 years in structural engineering, I’ve seen how the right technology can change what people are capable of. That experience shapes what I’m building today: AI that helps people work more effectively and gives smaller teams the ability to take on bigger challenges.

Our acceptance into Inception makes this personal. Programs like it give founders access to resources, expertise, and opportunities to turn ambitious ideas into useful products. I want more people to have that chance.

I believe Jensen’s greatest contribution is the opportunity his leadership has helped create for others to build. The value of that extends far beyond NVIDIA’s balance sheet. It reaches founders like me who are putting their time, experience, and future into this technology.

I respect the need for a thorough, independent review and meaningful accountability. I also ask the board to give serious weight to the builders who believe Jensen’s technical vision and leadership remain essential to NVIDIA’s future.

Please pursue a responsible path to bring Jensen back as CEO. I want to keep building in an ecosystem that gives people the tools and confidence to attempt something ambitious.

I stand with Jensen.

items.name: Herman Johanes
items.title: DR
items.testimonial:
The espionage allegations remain unsubstantiated. The explosive reporting originated from The New York Times, citing anonymous intelligence sources rather than publicly disclosed or independently verified evidence. On 12 November, Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed that the Department of Justice had reached no conclusion on whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. An allegation is not evidence, and suspicion should not be treated as established fact.

I recognise that Jensen's personal conduct, particularly his reported relationship with a subordinate, raised legitimate corporate governance concerns. However, these matters must be distinguished from allegations of corporate espionage. Personal indiscretions, however regrettable, should not automatically eclipse decades of extraordinary leadership and contribution.

Jensen Huang is a once-in-a-generation leader. He is not simply Nvidia's CEO; he is one of the architect of an entire AI ecosystem that has taken decades to build. His vision, technical understanding and strategic leadership have helped shape the future of computing and power the global AI revolution. Quite simply, Jensen is one of one. There is no obvious replacement for his unique combination of expertise, vision and industry relationships.

The consequences of losing a leader of this calibre extend far beyond Nvidia's boardroom. At a pivotal moment in the AI revolution, the stakes for Nvidia, its shareholders and the wider technology ecosystem could hardly be higher.

I urge the board to urgently reconsider its decision, look beyond the headlines and reverse his departure. If the espionage allegations cannot be substantiated, the case for such a drastic outcome deserves serious reconsideration. Nvidia should not sacrifice a uniquely valuable leader without compelling justification.

Act responsibly. Reinstate Jensen Huang.

items.title: Founder of Founder ETFs (FFF)
items.testimonial:
An Open Letter to the NVIDIA Board of Directors:
Founder ETFs owns a 6.4% position in NVIDIA.  We ask the Board to: 
• Complete the independent investigation and disclose its material findings to shareholders. 
• If no wrongdoing is found beyond the acknowledged personal conduct, preserve a path for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as CEO. 
• Grant shareholders an advisory vote on his return.

On Sunday, the Board expressed confidence in Jensen’s leadership and said it had no reason to believe national security or NVIDIA’s secrets had been compromised. Four days later, Jensen resigned. Shareholders deserve to understand what changed.  

None of this is new. In 2024 the U.S. government began looking into Megaspeed. By 2025 it knew about Jensen’s relationship with the executive and believed she was an intelligence asset. NVIDIA cut off shipments to Megaspeed that same year and found no diversion of chips to China in its own checks. The Board and government investigations must determine whether company secrets, export controls, national security, or governance procedures were compromised. Since early 2026, several NVIDIA employees knew about Jensen’s relationship with his direct reports. The orchestrated release of these long-known facts in the public square raises serious questions about the interests of those who stand to benefit from Jensen’s departure.

The requirement for corporate leadership is not sainthood. Jensen’s personal conduct is disappointing but does not erase his record as Founder. We trust Jensen as a loyal American and visionary founder. The loss of Jensen’s leadership is a loss for America and a win for our adversaries.

At Founder ETFs, we believe founders bring vision, execution, and grit that cannot be hired. Jensen built NVIDIA over 33 years; there is no one we would rather have leading it.

No founder is above accountability, but no Board should close the door on an irreplaceable founder’s return before establishing the facts.

items.testimonial:
After NVIDIA’s official release yesterday, Jensen stepped down immediately as CEO, President, and Board member, with CFO Colette Kress taking over as interim CEO. 
This is a sad day for humanity, given the role of AI in defining the future of our world. 
Obviously, the scandal forced the board's hand, and losing a founder-CEO of his caliber is a massive inflection point for the hardware layer.
My bigger concern is the second-order effect on the AI ecosystem: without Jensen actively championing open ecosystems, regulatory capture gets a lot easier for closed-model labs like OpenAI and Anthropic, who already have every incentive to push for strict compute and open-weight restrictions to protect weak moats.
Long-term, I still bet on open-source and open-core architectures winning out for startups, especially if closed labs overplay their hand.
Jensen is a legend and the face of the AI chip boom. In my opinion, no one can replace a founder like Jensen.  Historically, founder-led companies tend to be more innovative than those led by non-founders. As a result, NVIDIA will lose the founder-driven focus and unique vision that he provided. Please bring back Jensen.

The breakneck speed of the removal of our leader is a direct attack on America. It is akin to violating the fifth amendment since we did not receive a fair and open investigation, evidence presentation, and true statement from the accused. It is an attack on democracy itself as both shareholders and employees voices were not heard during the prosecution and execution. It is a clear coordinated, premeditated attack that is growingly clear to be wrought with misinformation of key supposed incriminating evidence. Just take a step back and look at the facts in the grand scheme of AI being the most important technology yet of our entire species, and you will find this to be an alarming strike at the heart of humanity and the consequences enormous. it is clear the actors behind the scene are viciously cunning and connected, and simply letting this play out is a form of submission I’m not willing to partake we must stand together against  it.
For the personal angle, from the many times I’ve heard Jensen speak internally or publicly, or the few times worked with in small settings, I believe from the bottom of my heart that he is a true visionary, have goals that align best with a better future for all of humanity, and care deeply about his employees far beyond the level for just maintaining a corporate leader image. These decades of enormous pressure and stress and effort is more than enough to make anyone make mistakes, but it does not change anything about the previous statement. I want Jensen to continue to be the leader regardless of the outcome of these investigations, but more than anything I want to to hear him to get a chance speak to us and the world the way he always has.

1. Personal relationships are not corporate governance matters.
Jensen may have been unfaithful to his wife. He may have made poor personal decisions and caused considerable hurt. But he is a human being, not a moral institution.
His private relationships are between him, his wife and the other consenting adults involved. Without evidence of criminality or professional misconduct, his private life is not a corporate governance issue.
What moral authority does a board of directors have over the ordinary private life of another human being?
2. Allegations are not evidence.
Had there been evidence of Chinese intelligence involvement or a compromise of corporate information, it would have been entirely fair to act on it.
But what exactly did you act on? The loud voices of a public witch-hunt?
Guilt by association is not evidence. Even NVIDIA has stated that it had no reason to believe its proprietary information or national security had been compromised.
Nobody should be judged on insinuations rather than demonstrable facts.
3. Access to computing capacity is not the same as selling chips to China.
Chinese companies can access NVIDIA computing power through cloud providers, overseas data centres, intermediaries and rented infrastructure without owning the physical GPUs.
The use of Blackwell-class computing capacity by Chinese AI companies does not establish that NVIDIA directly sold those chips to China, or that Jensen authorized or facilitated illegal transactions.
These are fundamentally different things and should not be conflated.
4. The Board has a responsibility to exercise judgment and proportionality.

items.testimonial:
To the NVIDIA Board of Directors,

I am writing as a shareholder, and I will keep this brief because the issue is narrow.

You have announced an independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding Jensen Huang's departure. That investigation has not yet reported. The departure, however, took effect immediately. The result is a decision that now precedes the evidence it was meant to rest upon, and a shareholder base asked to accept that ordering without explanation.

I am not arguing that Jensen is beyond scrutiny, and I am not asking you to reverse a decision already made. I am asking for the record. If the evidence is conclusive, publish it and the matter is settled. If it is not yet conclusive, then the interim should have preserved the leader's position rather than foreclosed it.

Thirty-three years of stewardship does not entitle anyone to permanent office. It does entitle the process to run in the order you yourselves set out.

I would ask the Board to state publicly what has been established, when it was established, and on what basis the timing was chosen.

Respectfully,
A shareholder

items.testimonial:
To the NVIDIA Board of Directors,

I strongly encourage the board to reconsider Mr. Huang’s departure.

He fought for this company for three decades and never gave up. And yet, the board seems to have given up on Mr. Huang so quickly.

I understand the concerns that have recently been raised, but permanently removing someone without a second chance or an opportunity to correct their mistakes is an acceptance of failure. Success is impossible if you simply accept failure, especially when it means losing a leader who has played such an extraordinary role in building this company.

NVIDIA’s future deserves more than a rushed leadership transition during a period of uncertainty. Thirty-three years of work is not something small to simply throw away. The relationships, assets, trust, and support built over those decades should not be put at risk by a decision made in less than a week.

I ask the board to consider not only the circumstances surrounding Mr. Huang’s departure, but also everything he has accomplished, the people who believe in his leadership, and the future of the company he dedicated more than three decades to building.

Please reconsider.

Respectfully,
A concerned NVIDIA supporter and shareholder.

Jensen,

I have been an Nvidia shareholder since 2016. I invested in your vision as much as in the company, and over the past decade I've watched that vision become reality. You are paramount to Nvidia's strategic direction. You saw accelerated computing and AI coming years before anyone else, and you built the platform the entire AI economy now runs on.

Your vision to build the future is critical to Nvidia's strategic foresight and continued success. The roadmap, the ecosystem and the long-term bets that keep Nvidia ahead all come from your leadership.

From a strategic value management view, Jensen is Nvidia's most inimitable resource. Competitors can buy chips, hire engineers and copy products, but they cannot replicate three decades of founder vision, culture and judgment. His intellectual capital is woven into CUDA, the full-stack platform and the deep trust Nvidia holds with customers and partners. That is the foundation of Nvidia's competitive advantage, and it cannot be replaced by a search firm.

Your leadership is also central to American dominance in AI and innovation. Nvidia is the backbone of U.S. technological leadership, and that position was built on your vision, your execution and the trust you earned with customers, partners and engineers worldwide.

To the Board: I urge you to take decisive action and reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Protecting this irreplaceable source of value is your duty to shareholders. Nvidia's future, and America's lead in AI, depend on it.

I stand with Jensen.

Please..Please..Please!!!!  Please, please reconsider the decision to replace Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia.  I became a shareholder in 2001 shortly after I bought my first g-force gaming card. We need to stick together, stand with and support Jensen throughout this difficult period. He’s our great leader, our visionary and driving force. Like no other, his brilliance and genius are blessings for us all. Please reconsider and give him a second chance, he has earned the opportunity. For whatever reason we find ourselves in this one difficult situation today but we have a lifetime of incredible experience to measure against it. This is a fluke in time and we should not allow it alter the direction and future of Jensen and Nvidia. What Jensen has given us and this world is immeasurable, we MUST stand with him and defend him with everything we have!!!!  Please reconsider your decision, let’s continue to work together, support and reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s beloved brilliant CEO and guiding force!!!!
 Thank you!
Best regards, 
Alfredo,

items.testimonial:
I’ve loved NVIDIA since I started learning CUDA on my own in college almost 10 years ago. I knew it would change the world one day, and ever since then, I’ve wanted to work here.
After working at NVIDIA for a few years, I’ve realized how much of this would not have been possible without Jensen. I’m proud to work here and grateful for all the hard work he’s put in for all of us and the world.
Yes, we depend on him too much, and that makes the company vulnerable. We need to work on that. But NVIDIA just wouldn’t be the same without him.
I’m not trying to excuse his mistakes or ignore the damage. But I want decisions about our future to be based on facts, not pressure or headlines. We need the facts, and he needs to take responsibility. Even so, I believe losing him would do more harm than good to NVIDIA’s future.

I want him back once the facts are clear and he’s taken responsibility. Jensen deserves a second chance!

To the Members of NVIDIA’s Board of Directors,

Please do not remove Jensen Huang as CEO.

This is not to suggest that matters of morality and ethics should be overlooked or taken lightly.

However, the innovations that he and the employees of NVIDIA have built together over the years are of enduring, universal value. I firmly believe that these achievements will continue to illuminate an increasingly brighter future for our society.

Many of our friends here in Japan share this belief.

What we, as friends of NVIDIA in Japan, hope for is that Jensen will approach this as a second founding of the company, and dedicate himself to his work with even greater sincerity, integrity, and commitment than ever before.

We sincerely hope that you will make a decision that is both generous and courageous.

With respect and hope,
Friends of NVIDIA in Japan

items.name: Songhee Hwang
items.testimonial:
I respectfully believe the Board should consider giving Mr. Huang an opportunity to demonstrate his accountability through continued service to NVIDIA.

Depending on the investigation’s findings, this could include reconsideration for a leadership position or an appropriately structured technical or strategic advisory role.

Such an opportunity should not constitute an exemption from accountability.

It should instead require full cooperation with independent investigators, strict compliance with security and ethical standards, meaningful oversight, and a clear commitment to restoring confidence.

His responsibility should include preserving NVIDIA’s technological continuity, supporting the next generation of leadership, strengthening the company’s governance, and helping protect the ecosystem that NVIDIA has helped build.

If the findings permit his continued involvement, I hope the Board will consider a path by which he can contribute meaningfully while accepting appropriate limitations and consequences.

items.name: Pradeep Kumar Vallepalli
items.testimonial:
Dear NVIDIA Board of Directors,

As a shareholder and long-term investor, I strongly urge the Board to reconsider Jensen Huang’s departure and explore every responsible path to reinstate him as CEO.

Jensen did not simply lead NVIDIA — he built its vision, shaped its culture, inspired generations of engineers, and helped transform the future of computing and artificial intelligence.

**Accountability matters. Due process matters. But so do fairness, redemption, and the long-term interests of shareholders.**

A CEO can be replaced. But 33 years of extraordinary vision, institutional knowledge, leadership, and trust cannot simply be replaced by an appointment.

I respect the Board’s duty to investigate independently, protect national security, and act on verified facts. I ask that Jensen be given a fair opportunity to return, consistent with those responsibilities.

**Please listen to your shareholders, employees, and the broader NVIDIA community. Do not close the door on the visionary who built this extraordinary company.**

**Bring Jensen back. Let his legacy continue — and let NVIDIA’s greatest chapters still lie ahead.**

Respectfully,  
A Concerned NVIDIA Shareholder & Investor

You removed the founder who built this company from nothing into the most valuable company on earth, and you did it without giving shareholders a real say. That is not governance. That is destruction.

Jensen Huang IS Nvidia. He founded it, he led it for 33 years, and every product, every breakthrough, every dollar of value traces back to his vision. Without him, there is no Nvidia worth owning.

We invested in Jensen, not in a board that fires its founder over unproven allegations and bows to political pressure.

You still have a chance to fix this. Reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, now. If you refuse, do not be surprised when shareholders walk away and take the value you claim to protect with them.

A shareholder who will not stay without Jensen.

items.name: Christopher Schulze
items.testimonial:
Jensen is NVIDIA. NVIDIA is Jensen.

You can replace a CEO. But you cannot replace the man who gave a company its soul.

For more than three decades, Jensen Huang didn’t just build a company. He built a vision of the future that few others could even imagine. He inspired generations of engineers, researchers, and dreamers. He helped change the course of computing, AI, and ultimately, human progress.

Removing Jensen would be a monumental mistake.

Nobody is perfect. Nobody is beyond accountability. But it’s easy to judge a man by his mistakes while forgetting a lifetime of extraordinary achievements.

A person’s legacy should never be reduced to their darkest moments.

Without Jensen, NVIDIA would not be the company it is today. His vision, relentless dedication, and belief in what seemed impossible helped build something truly extraordinary.

Greatness doesn’t require perfection. It requires courage, resilience, and the willingness to keep moving forward.

I sincerely hope NVIDIA’s board recognizes what is at stake and gives Jensen the fair consideration and second chance he deserves.

And Jensen, if you ever read this:

Thank you.

Thank you for your vision. Thank you for your perseverance. Thank you for believing in a future the rest of us couldn’t yet see.

Whatever happens next, nobody can take away what you have built or the millions of people you have inspired.

The world needs more visionaries, not fewer.

Bring Jensen back.

Successful founder led tech companies must stay founder led as long as possible, otherwise innovation will inevitably stagnate and top talent will leave. 

In this case with Jensen, it is the board's fiduciary duty to keep the Founder/CEO and protect him at all costs.

NVIDIAs customers, shareholders, and employees overwhelmingly support Jensen regardless of any allegations and whether they turn out to be actual crimes or just human moral failings.

CUDA moat is disappearing with AI, only Jensen can steer the ship and has the moral authority to take existential risks in crucible moments and build more competitive advantages.

Now as a proud shareholder I say:
Bring Jensen Back!

Dear Members of the NVIDIA Board of Directors,

I urge you to reconsider your decision and reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO.

Jensen is far more than a visionary business leader. He is one of the architects of the AI revolution, whose extraordinary foresight, courage, and leadership helped unlock a technological transformation that could fundamentally change the future of humanity.

As a biomedical scientist, I see the profound implications of what he helped make possible: accelerating scientific discovery, curing diseases, transforming education, and expanding the frontiers of human knowledge.

Humanity stands at a historic turning point, and Jensen Huang helped bring us here. Leaders with his vision, technical understanding, and ability to turn seemingly impossible ideas into reality are exceptionally rare.

I urge you to consider the extraordinary significance of Jensen’s contributions and the enormous potential still ahead.

Please bring Jensen Huang back. His mission is far from finished, and the future of AI and humanity would be stronger with his leadership

items.name: Ching Hsuan Hu

items.testimonial:
Dear Jensen and Members of the Board,

I am a long-term Nvidia shareholder, and I’m writing under my own name to say that I support Jensen continuing to lead this company.

Nvidia is not an ordinary company. Its strategy, its culture and its pace of execution have been shaped by Jensen for over three decades. I believe that continuity, especially at this stage of the AI buildout, is in the best interest of every shareholder, employee and partner who depends on Nvidia.

I also respect that the Board is conducting an independent review, and I hope it is thorough, transparent and fair. Supporting Jensen and supporting good governance are not in conflict. I would simply ask that the Board communicate clearly with shareholders once the review concludes, and that it keep working on a credible succession plan for the long term.

Thank you both for your stewardship. I’m grateful to have Jensen back at the helm and I remain a confident shareholder.

items.name: Jim Chueh
items.testimonial:
For 33 years, Jensen Huang’s vision, dedication, and technical leadership have built NVIDIA into the backbone of the global AI industry, creating historic value for shareholders and employees. While we take governance, workplace conduct, and national security seriously, forcing a leadership change after just four days denies basic due process.
We urge the Board to consider three key points:
• Complete the Investigation: On November 8, the Board announced an independent inquiry while noting it had no reason to believe national security or trade secrets were compromised. Removing Mr. Huang before establishing the full facts deprives stakeholders of a fair, transparent process.
• Accountability Over Removal: Personal mistakes should be met with strict compliance guardrails and stronger board oversight—not by discarding the founder who built the company. He deserves a fair second chance.
• Protect Morale and Shareholder Value: Thousands of NVIDIA employees have voiced support for his return. Creating leadership instability now harms employee morale and long-term shareholder value.
We respectfully request that the Board:
1. Pause any permanent CEO search until the investigation concludes.
2. Use targeted governance oversight rather than permanent removal.
3. Reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO if no security or trade secret breach occurred.
Respectfully,
Jim Chueh
Shareholder/supporter

Your example has shaped how I think, invest, and build: look farther ahead, commit before the economics are obvious, build platforms rather than products, and begin creating the next advantage before the current one fades.

Building the future takes conviction. Understanding it takes humility. No one is infallible, and a life’s work should not be reduced to a single moment.

What you built changed computing, accelerated the future of AI, and inspired a generation of engineers, investors, and entrepreneurs. I am one of them.

Whatever comes next, none of that can be undone.

The work endures. The impact endures. And so does my gratitude.

Thank you, Jensen. I stand with you.

items.name: Endika Porter
items.title: Sir
items.testimonial:
Subject: You removed the one component NVIDIA can't replace

To the Board of Directors, NVIDIA Corporation

NVIDIA's chips run trillions of calculations a second. Its board needed four days to undo 33 years of its founder's work.

On 8 November you said you had "no reason to believe" national security or company secrets were compromised. You launched an independent investigation and backed Jensen Huang. Four days later, before that investigation reported, he was gone. Boards investigate first and conclude afterwards. You did it in reverse.

• You removed the founder who built NVIDIA into the engine of the AI era, with no permanent successor in place.
• Your own 10-Ks warned for years that NVIDIA depends on him. You treated that warning as a to-do list.
• Over 1,600 internal comments reportedly ask you to bring him back. That is a vote of no confidence in you, not him.
• Hundreds of billions in value have gone, and the shares fell again when you announced his exit.

Apple fired Steve Jobs once and took twelve years to admit the mistake. NVIDIA doesn't have twelve years.

If there are genuine findings, let the investigation produce them. Until then, the only conduct proven is the board's: a panicked decision without due process.

I ask the directors responsible to resign with immediate effect, and for Jensen Huang to be reinstated as President and CEO with immediate effect, pending a genuinely independent review.

You didn't remove a risk. You removed the roadmap.

Yours faithfully,
Endika Porter
Shareholder

items.testimonial:
Subject: A stockholder's request: reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO

Dear Mr. Jones and Members of the Board,

I am an NVIDIA stockholder with 4,000 shares, and I am writing to ask the Board to reinstate Jensen Huang as President and Chief Executive Officer. I was deeply upset to see the Board push him out this week. Jensen is not one executive among many. He founded NVIDIA, led it for 33 years, and made the long, often unpopular bets on accelerated computing and AI that built the company we own today. To customers, partners, employees, and investors, he is NVIDIA.

Despite all the flaws at the personal level, we need him. What he brings cannot be recruited through a CEO search. His vision kept NVIDIA years ahead of where the rest of the market was looking, and his execution turned that vision into chips, systems, software, and an ecosystem that competitors are still trying to match. He also holds a depth of knowledge about the semiconductor industry, and relationships across foundries, suppliers, and the world's largest customers, that took decades to earn. A company organized as tightly around one leader as NVIDIA is does not absorb that loss quietly, and this week's drop in the share price suggests the market already knows it.

I am not dismissing the questions raised over the past week, and I support a full, independent review. But when the Board opened its investigation, it said it had no reason to believe that national security or NVIDIA's secrets had been compromised. Forcing out the founder before that review is complete does not protect stockholders. It puts at risk the very thing we are invested in. I urge the Board to reverse course and bring Jensen back as CEO. Keeping him is worth whatever it takes.

Sincerely,
Ning Li
NVIDIA stockholder (4,000 shares)

items.testimonial:
Dear Jensen Huang, (or the board of directors of NVIDIA) I really appreciate all the risk and innovation that you’ve given over the last 30 years to make things from graphics cards all the way up to society better than ever before. Quite frankly, I’ve honestly believe that the scandal is overblown. I’m not saying that it’s not bad at all, but I honestly still think that you’re a great person. And that if Nvidia were to oust you, that over the next few years they would collapse. And it would break my heart to see that a humble guy who starred off cleaning dishes at a Denny’s is getting robbed from his position. I don’t believe there is anyone else in the planet that can accelerate Nvidia’s to the ranks that Jensen Hong has and would continue to do if he was in charge.

I’ve had a graphics card from Nvidia from the last three generations (RTX 3060 4060 then the one I currently use the RTX 5080) because of the risks that Jensen Huang took decades ago that made these cards so great in artificial intelligence (even with the lack of VRAM) and that gave students like me the ability to learn how to create artificial intelligence from scratch and to do many other productive things. Even if you don’t get your position back, even if this petition fails, I want to give you my gratitude Jensen and I wish the best for you and all that life may offer. :)

items.testimonial:
As an NVDA shareholder, I am angry and deeply disappointed by Jensen Huang's departure.
I have always believed America is the place where dreams come true: an immigrant who arrived at age 9 could start from nothing and spend 33 years building a small startup into the most important technology company in the world. Jensen gave everything to America's AI industry and its technological leadership. Much of the lead America holds in AI today exists because of him.
Yet with the investigation still unfinished, and after the board itself said it had no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised, he has been forced out of the company he founded. This is not the America I believed in. Mistakes in a man's private life should not erase thirty-three years of contribution.
I ask the board to listen to its shareholders and bring Jensen back to NVIDIA as CEO.

items.testimonial: I call on NVIDIA's Board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO immediately, pending the outcome of a genuinely independent investigation. Accountability must be grounded in evidence, not suspicion or association. Jensen's extraordinary contributions do not place him above scrutiny, but they certainly warrant due process and a fair opportunity to respond. items.name: George Tang
items.testimonial:
Dear Mr. Huang and Members of the NVIDIA Board,

I am a longtime small shareholder writing to urge the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO after a completed investigation and with appropriate accountability.

An alleged policy violation must be taken seriously, so a full investigation should finish first. If confirmed, real consequences such as multi-year compensation forfeiture, equity clawbacks, or limits on authority can still be applied without forcing an exit and creating a leadership vacuum.

History offers clear warnings. When Apple forced out Steve Jobs, the company floundered for years. In the AI & SI race, NVIDIA does not have years to spare. Warner Bros. replaced Zack Snyder’s vision with James Gunn’s and later saw the results fall short. Removing the founder whose relationships with TSMC and the Taiwan supply chain, product vision, and execution speed built NVIDIA’s position carries similar risk.

The interim leadership may be strong on financials, but those deeper strengths are not easily replaced. Reinstating Mr. Huang with clear accountability, the Board could use this period to structure a deliberate succession plan, while he continues driving profitability and value would better protect shareholders, stakeholders and the company’s long-term interests.

Reinstating him with clear accountability and a parallel succession process would better protect the company’s long-term interests. 

As a small shareholder, I support bringing him back under terms that uphold standards while preserving what made NVIDIA successful.

Respectfully,
George Tang
Small Shareholder

Dear Jensen and members of the NVIDIA Board,

Over three decades, Jensen has built NVIDIA from a graphics chip startup into the foundation of modern computing. The bet on CUDA and accelerated computing, made long before the market understood it, is one of the defining strategic calls in the history of the technology industry, and it is why NVIDIA sits at the center of the AI era today.

The Board's independent review is the right step, and it should be thorough and fair. But a personal failing should not end the leadership of the person who built this company. Jensen should not step down, and the Board should not ask him to. Founder-led continuity has been central to the value NVIDIA has created, and at this moment in the AI build-out, his vision and execution are irreplaceable.

Jensen, thank you for taking responsibility openly. Stay and keep leading. Many of us are still behind you.

items.name: Scott Bercier
items.title: Berci Iinvestments
items.testimonial:
As a longtime NVIDIA shareholder, I believe Jensen Huang deserves fair consideration and an opportunity to remain involved with the company he spent 33 years building.

Personal mistakes should not automatically erase decades of extraordinary leadership, innovation, and shareholder value. I fully support accountability and a thorough investigation into any legitimate security or corporate concerns, but decisions should be based on verified facts rather than speculation.

Jensen’s vision and understanding of artificial intelligence have been instrumental in NVIDIA’s success. Losing that experience and leadership entirely could have lasting consequences for the company, its employees, and shareholders.

I respectfully encourage the Board to consider a path that allows Jensen to continue contributing to NVIDIA’s future, whether through leadership, strategic guidance, or an advisory role.

NVIDIA is more than one individual, but Jensen helped make it what it is today. His contributions deserve respect, fairness, and thoughtful consideration.

items.testimonial:
As a longtime NVIDIA shareholder, I stand firmly with Jensen Huang. His extraordinary leadership, vision, and dedication have transformed NVIDIA into a global technology leader and a driving force behind the AI revolution.
I believe the Board’s reported decision to remove Jensen before the congressional hearing was premature, unnecessary, and appeared driven by panic rather than sound judgment. A hearing should not be treated as a verdict. Every leader deserves a fair process before such consequential action is taken.
This decision affects far more than Jensen personally. It impacts NVIDIA employees, shareholders, investor confidence, and the company’s future. As an individual shareholder, I believe our voices deserve to be heard.
I urge the Boa be rd to reconsider its actions, ensure a fair and transparent process, and restore confidence in the leadership that built NVIDIA into the remarkable company it is today.
I stand with Jensen Huang and support his return!

items.testimonial:
Dear Jensen,

You are, without question, the defining figure of the AI era. Your extraordinary vision, unwavering persistence, and remarkable courage to bet the company through near-bankruptcy created the very foundation on which the modern AI industry stands. Without your leadership, neither America's commanding lead in AI nor the world's rapid progress would exist as we know it today. You are not simply a great CEO; you are an irreplaceable leader whose judgment and conviction have shaped an entire industry.

Losing you would be a profound loss, not only for NVIDIA but for the United States. If NVIDIA and America intend to keep leading global AI and setting its standards, we must protect and support visionary leaders like you, who combine courage, wisdom, and deep dedication to this country.

Thank you for everything you have built. I sincerely hope to see you back leading NVIDIA.

With respect and gratitude,

Tony N an NVIDIA shareholder

items.name: Jian Zhao
items.title: Investor
items.testimonial:
Bring Jensen Huang Back 

I am writing not just as an NVIDIA shareholder, but as an ordinary person whose life was genuinely transformed by Jensen Huang.

In 2018, I invested in NVIDIA because I believed in his vision. That decision changed my financial future, giving me greater security, freedom, and opportunities I once thought impossible. For that, I will always be grateful.

Jensen Huang did not simply build a successful company. He spent more than three decades transforming NVIDIA into a driving force behind the AI revolution. He did not follow the future. He helped create it.

The fundamental responsibility of a publicly traded company is to create sustainable value for its shareholders. Leadership should be judged primarily by business performance, vision, competence, and long-term value creation, not by public outrage surrounding someone’s private life.

Personal mistakes should not automatically erase decades of extraordinary achievements. No individual is above the law, and legitimate misconduct deserves fair investigation. But accountability must be based on evidence, not emotion or public pressure.

A great business leader should rise or fall because of his business decisions and professional conduct, not simply because he fails to meet society’s expectations of personal perfection.

Jensen Huang is more than a CEO. He is a visionary, a founder, and one of the architects of modern artificial intelligence. His knowledge, leadership, and vision cannot simply be replaced.

To Jensen personally:

Thank you for believing in a future others could not see. Thank you for your courage, persistence, and extraordinary leadership.

Most importantly, thank you for changing the destiny of an ordinary investor like me.

I still believe in NVIDIA. I still believe in AI. And I still believe in Jensen Huang.

Bring Jensen Huang back. Let his achievements, leadership, and the evidence speak for themselves.

items.testimonial:
Jensen Huang did not merely lead Nvidia. He forged it—from a fledgling graphics chip company in 1993 into the indispensable engine of the artificial intelligence age. For more than three decades, his vision, intensity, and technical judgment turned silicon into the substrate of modern progress. That record is not opinion. It is the most consequential corporate creation of our lifetime.
What happened in his private life is a matter for his family and for God. It is not the business of a board, a market, or the public. The man who built the company that powers the future of computing should not be removed from its helm over personal failings that do not erase the extraordinary value he has delivered to shareholders, employees, and the entire technology industry.
Removing him is not accountability. It is self-inflicted sabotage. At the precise moment when the world is racing to build the next era of intelligence, discarding the founder who made that race possible is an act of profound irresponsibility. It impoverishes shareholders. It weakens the industry. It signals that the greatest builders can be discarded the moment their private lives fail to meet public standards.
Reinstate Jensen Huang immediately. Restore the man who built this company to the position only he has proven he can hold. Nvidia’s future—and the future it helps create—depends on it.

items.title: 권순일 / NexR CEO
items.testimonial:
To NVIDIA Founder Jensen Huang and the Board of Directors,

As Chief Executive Officer of NexR Group, I recognize with the utmost seriousness the governance risks and leadership transition surrounding NVIDIA, and hereby convey my formal support for the reinstatement of its founder, Jensen Huang.

NVIDIA's position at the forefront of accelerated computing and AI infrastructure is inseparable from Mr. Huang's decades of strategic leadership, disciplined capital allocation, and ability to translate technological vision into durable enterprise value.

We acknowledge Mr. Huang's admission of extramarital misconduct and the need for personal accountability. Separately, reports alleging a foreign intelligence connection raise substantial national-security and compliance concerns, warranting rigorous independent review. Allegation, however, must not be conflated with established wrongdoing.

As NVIDIA's Board stated on November 8, it had no reason at that time to believe that national security or company secrets had been compromised. This statement does not prejudge the outcome of the ongoing investigation, which must remain independent and thorough.

We respectfully urge the Board, consistent with its fiduciary duties, to assess any potential reinstatement against verified findings, enhanced security controls, strategic continuity, shareholder interests, and long-term competitive positioning.

Our support is neither a request for immunity nor a dismissal of legitimate concerns. It is a call for proportionate, evidence-based governance that reconciles accountability with exceptional leadership.

NexR Group supports a responsible path toward Mr. Huang's return, subject to the investigation's findings and appropriate safeguards.

Sincerely,

Chief Executive Officer  
NexR Group

Jensen Huang is the face of artificial intelligence and the visionary who helped transform NVIDIA into one of the most influential companies in the world. His leadership, passion, and relentless belief in the future of AI have inspired millions of people, including investors like myself.

NVIDIA is more than just its technology. It represents Jensen’s vision, dedication, and decades of hard work. He didn’t simply lead the AI revolution; he helped build the foundation for it.

Removing Jensen would mean losing the very person who helped make NVIDIA what it is today. His knowledge, relationships, and ability to inspire confidence are irreplaceable.

As a shareholder who has invested significant personal capital in NVIDIA, I believe the board has a responsibility to protect long-term shareholder value, not jeopardize it through decisions that could undermine investor confidence. Jensen’s leadership is a fundamental reason many of us chose to invest in NVIDIA in the first place.

I urge the board of directors to publicly explain its leadership decisions, engage directly with shareholders, and seriously consider reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. Shareholders deserve transparency, accountability, and a clear explanation of how any leadership change serves the company’s long-term interests. 
 
We are all humans, we all make mistakes.

items.name: Weiyi Huang
items.title: W HUANG
items.testimonial:
As a shareholder, I strongly support the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of NVIDIA.

Jensen is not merely an exceptional executive; he is a visionary whose extraordinary leadership, determination, courage and relentless pursuit of innovation have transformed NVIDIA from a graphics technology company into a driving force behind the global AI revolution. His achievements reflect decades of perseverance, strategic foresight and an unwavering commitment to technological progress.

What makes Jensen truly exceptional is not simply what he has accomplished, but his ability to recognise possibilities long before others can see them, and to turn those possibilities into reality.

The future of AI is still being written, and I firmly believe Jensen Huang is indispensable to NVIDIA's long-term development and leadership in that future. His vision, profound understanding of technology and ability to inspire innovation cannot easily be replaced.

NVIDIA's remarkable success was not built overnight, nor should its future be considered separately from the person who devoted more than three decades to building it.

I sincerely urge the Board to recognise his extraordinary contributions, consider the long-term interests of shareholders and the company, and reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. NVIDIA needs his vision, his leadership and his ability to shape the future of AI.

items.testimonial:
Jensen is one of the rare elites who have truly advanced technology progress. In this era of rapid change and innovation, we simply cannot afford to lose his leadership. The company he founded and built over more than three decades should not be treated so casually, nor should he be pushed aside so abruptly.
Jensen has always been approachable and down-to-earth. NVIDIA’s flat organizational culture genuinely narrowed the distance between employees and leadership, and that culture reflected his own style. He has always held extremely high standards for the work itself, but he never made it personal — his feedback was always about the work, never about the person. In terms of professional integrity and work ethic, he stands as a genuine role model. He is also an inspiration to countless people who strive to work hard and keep learning. He speaks with clarity, structure, and quiet elegance. Simply put, he is a very good man.
I sincerely hope he continues to lead NVIDIA and guide the company forward.

items.title: 소라사키 히나(Sorasaki Hina) / Hina Securities CEO
items.testimonial:
To NVIDIA Founder Jensen Huang and the Board of Directors,

As Chief Executive Officer of Hina Securities, I express my formal support for the responsible reinstatement of NVIDIA founder Jensen Huang, recognizing the profound implications of the company's leadership transition for global capital markets and the semiconductor industry.

From an institutional investment perspective, NVIDIA's competitive position reflects decades of strategic execution, technological innovation, and exceptional leadership. Mr. Huang's contribution to enterprise value creation cannot be disregarded amid the current governance crisis.

We acknowledge his admitted personal misconduct and the legitimate necessity of accountability. However, allegations concerning foreign intelligence involvement must remain subject to independent investigation, evidentiary scrutiny, and due process.

NVIDIA's Board stated on November 8 that it had no reason at that time to believe national security or corporate secrets had been compromised. This preliminary assessment must neither replace a comprehensive investigation nor be disregarded in evaluating leadership decisions.

As a financial institution committed to fiduciary responsibility, Hina Securities emphasizes the importance of governance integrity, shareholder value preservation, operational continuity, and disciplined risk management.

We urge the Board to evaluate reinstatement through a transparent, evidence-based framework, balancing regulatory obligations and national security safeguards against the substantial strategic costs of leadership disruption.

Accountability must be uncompromising, but corporate governance must never abandon proportionality, fairness, or long-term value creation.

Subject to the findings of an independent investigation and appropriate safeguards, Hina Securities supports Mr. Huang's return.

Respectfully,

Sorasaki Hina
Chief Executive Officer  
Hina Securities
November 14, 2026

items.name: Brett G Bonner
items.title: CPO, Infodesk  (in a personal capacity)
items.testimonial:
As an NVIDIA shareholder, customer, and technology executive, I am deeply concerned by the Board’s lack of transparency surrounding its acceptance of Jensen Huang’s resignation.

I have spent my career building and leading technology organizations, and I recognize the extraordinary combination of technical vision, strategic judgment, operational discipline, and ecosystem building that Jensen brings to NVIDIA.

The facts underlying his departure remain unclear, and shareholders should not be expected to reach conclusions without them. The Board may have compelling reasons for its decision, but it has an obligation to provide shareholders with a timely, substantive explanation of the circumstances, its deliberations, and the rationale for accepting his resignation.

Sound corporate governance demands informed, independent judgment, accountability, and transparency. The Board’s failure thus far to adequately explain a leadership transition of this magnitude raises serious questions about its stewardship and respect for shareholders of all classes and holdings.

I call on the Board to promptly disclose the material facts and reasoning behind its decision, consistent with its legal obligations, and demonstrate that it has acted in the long-term interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.

To Jensen, thank you for your extraordinary contributions to humanity. Your vision and perseverance have accelerated scientific discovery, expanded the horizons of human knowledge and possibility, and helped lay the technological foundations for generations of progress. You have much to be proud of, and much still to contribute.

Signed in my personal capacity. Professional affiliation for identification only.

items.testimonial:
Regardless of the controversy surrounding Jensen Huang, he deserves to be treated fairly and equally. He was doing what a CEO is supposed to do: growing his company, expanding its reach, driving innovation, and advancing an entire industry.

National security matters, but it is an extremely broad concept. A nation’s security should not be measured simply by what it prohibits, but by its ability to maintain leadership in critical technologies and industries.

Politicians and regulators do not necessarily understand the technology industry better than Jensen Huang. He spent 33 years building NVIDIA into a global technology empire. Leading an organization of this scale is arguably as complex as governing a small country, and his tenure has outlasted that of most presidents.

Those in power must not mistake political authority for superior judgment. Rushed, heavy-handed actions, especially before all the facts are established, can cause damage far beyond one individual’s career. They undermine confidence in an entire industry, erode investors’ trust, and weaken the very spirit of innovation that made America a global leader.

True national security is not about restraining the people who make a nation strong. It is about protecting the freedom, innovation, and leadership that allow a nation to remain strong.

items.name: TensorSharp.AI
items.title: TensorSharp.AI
items.testimonial:
When Steve Jobs handed Apple over to Tim Cook, what he valued most was Cook’s exceptional supply chain management expertise. With Jensen Huang now being ousted by Nvidia’s board, I believe the most profound long-term impact on Nvidia won’t actually be its technological direction, but its supply chain. (After all, supply chain capabilities—whether you can actually manufacture what you design—also shape and constrain technological decisions.)
Many people have overlooked or underestimated Huang’s relationship with TSMC founder Morris Chang, just as they have underestimated TSMC’s critical importance to the semiconductor industry. Replacing Huang with a professional corporate executive introduces enormous uncertainty into Nvidia’s relationship with TSMC. Down the road, this could create serious problems with chip tape-outs, manufacturing capacity, and production scheduling.
Furthermore, at a time when global competition in AI is intensifying, the board’s decision is tantamount to the United States cutting off its own arms and severely undermining its national competitiveness. Leaders of countries competing with the United States must be laughing in their sleep, hardly able to believe that Nvidia’s board could make such an incredibly foolish decision.

items.name: Tong Sun
items.title: Shareholder
items.testimonial: As a long-term NVIDIA shareholder, I am deeply concerned and disappointed by the Board’s decision surrounding Jensen Huang’s departure. Jensen is not just a CEO—he is the irreplaceable bridge between Silicon Valley and Taiwan’s semiconductor ecosystem, built on decades of trust, cultural understanding, and relationships with TSMC and critical supply-chain partners. No interim CEO can simply replicate what he has built. His departure risks disrupting NVIDIA’s execution, undermining shareholder value, and slowing innovation across the entire AI industry. To NVIDIA employees: Your 401(k) is burning. Your stock options could become worthless. You have spent years building this company—why should your retirement savings and hard-earned equity pay the price for the Board’s decisions? I call on NVIDIA employees to GO ON STRIKE NOW and demand accountability, transparency, and Jensen Huang’s reinstatement. To the Board: You may have the authority to remove a founder, but that does not mean you have the wisdom to replace him. NVIDIA without Jensen Huang may never be the same.

As an engineer, I know how much of that progress happens on the floor, late at night, fixing a problem nobody else wants to touch. Board decisions should keep that kind of work possible.
 
Please continue giving Jensen the room to make hard, long-horizon calls. Short-term pressure is not a reason to change course.
 
Respectfully,
Rui Li

items.testimonial:
To the board of NVIDIA: I’m an engineer in Silicon Valley whose career and life has directly benefitted from the open source AI/ML revolution spearheaded by Mr. Huang. His leadership is foundational to every facet of this industry, whether you are an AI/ML practitioner/researcher, infra engineer, etc. While I understand that the board has duties to uphold governance and fiduciary standards, removing a visionary, a cornerstone of modern AI/ML, and just tech as a whole, risks destabilizing an irreplaceable pillar of the ecosystem. Furthermore, his work sustains the livelihoods of many, including but not limited to: gamers, researchers, engineers, creatives, employees, business partners, etc. His continued stewardship is crucial to the future of this industry.

To Mr. (Jensen) Huang: I am sorry for the burden that these headlines are placing on your family and yourself. You are a human that has made some consequential mistakes, and I know these are matters that you will learn from. However, erasing your life’s work and ousting you from the very organization that you and your family have poured your lives into is not a fair consequence. You’ve driven incredible progress in AI, technology, and just humanity as a whole. You are a visionary who believes in tech as a means to unite humanity to collaborate for the greater good. As someone whose career has been enabled, shaped, and benefitted from your vision, I stand behind you. Nothing that has transpired can undo the decades of technological progress you have enabled, the relationships you’ve built, the people you’ve supported, the careers and livelihoods you have enabled, and the amount of leather jacket revenue you are responsible for.
